THIS MFA CROB IN MFA 9762/2018 IS FILED UNDER ORDER 41 RULE 22 OF CPC, READ WITH SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED:
30.08.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.868/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, KUNDAPURA, MEMBER,
ADDITIONAL MACT, KUNDAPURA, ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
THIS APPEAL, ALONG WITH MFA. CROB.

COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
An accident occurred on 18.06.2016 between a motorcycle, in which the claimant was riding pillion, and a Bolero pickup, which resulted in grievous injuries to the claimant.
2. The claimant, as a consequence, preferred a claim petition which has been allowed by the Tribunal and a sum of Rs.6,92,597/- is awarded and the insurer is made liable to pay the compensation.
3. Being aggrieved, the insurer is in appeal and so also the claimant.
The insurer contends that as on the date of the accident the claimant did not possess a licence to drive a transport vehicle and therefore, the fastening of liability on it was incorrect.

5. It is to be noticed here that the claimant did possess a light motor vehicle licence and he was,
therefore, authorized to drive even a transport vehicle which was having an unladen weight of 7,500 kgs., in light of the judgment rendered in Mukund Dewangan's1 case.

6. In light of the fact that in the present case the Bolero pickup vehicle was less than 7,500 kgs., the licence that was possessed was adequate to drive it and the liability cannot, therefore, be escaped by the Insurer.
Consequently, there is no merit in the appeal of the insurer and the same is dismissed insofar as liability is concerned.

sentences.text:
As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 20%,
though the doctor had assessed the disability of the particular limb at 24%.

In my view, since the claimant had suffered fracture of tibia and fibula and had suffered disability at 24% to the particular limb, it would be appropriate to treat the whole body disability at 15% and not 20%.
8.
The Tribunal has taken the notional income of the claimant as Rs.8,000/-, since there was no evidence to that effect.

As the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has determined the notional income as Rs.9,500/- for the accident of the year 2016, it would be appropriate to determine the notional income of the claimant at Rs.9,500/-.

9. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,90,700/- (Rs.9,500/- X 12 X '17' X 15%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.
NC: 2024:KHC:51013 10.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.75,000/-
towards 'pain and sufferings', Rs.30,000/- towards 'conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges' and Rs.75,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
The said sums are just and proper and are accordingly affirmed.
11. A sum of Rs.52,997/- is awarded towards 'medical expenses' and Rs.18,000/- is awarded towards 'future medical expenses'.
The same is just and proper and is accordingly affirmed.
12. The Tribunal has awarded a Rs.1,15,200/- towards 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
In my view, this amount would be incorrect.

As the claimant had suffered a fracture of tibia and fibula, it would be appropriate to treat the laid-up period as four months and consequently, the claimant would be entitled to only a sum of Rs.38,000/- (Rs.9,500/- X 4 months) towards loss of earnings during laid up period.
NC: 2024:KHC:51013 13.
Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
